title: 1-bit caption count inspection recomputes full-resolution masks on every Style-slider move
files: src/App.svelte:108 (set derived, new object per move)
workThatDisappears: For pattern/diffusion styles (Checker, Bayer, Hatch, Noise, Atkinson) and unsaturated pointwise samples on sampled sources up to 262144 px/frame, every input event restarts each tile's collection; the MessageChannel yield completes before the next pointermove, so a full-resolution mask per tile runs and is then discarded by the next move's abort.
frequency: Every range input event (~60/s) during a 1-bit Style-slider drag, per tile on the wall.
expectedBenefit: Smoother 1-bit slider drags on walls of medium sprites/sheets (e.g. 300^2-512^2) on phones: less main-thread CPU between moves, shorter input delay (a running mask is uninterruptible). Node host probe: 4 tiles x 60 moves at 512^2 -> Checker 222 masks / 628 ms, Atkinson 198 masks / 889 ms; collecting once after rest -> 4 masks / 10-37 ms.
proposedChange: In the Tile oneBit effect, read `budget`; after marking the retained result pending, return without starting collection while `budget > 0` and the current tile mask is sampled (untracked `mw !== item.img.w || mh !== item.img.h`). When the drag rests (sliderDrag reports false after 150 ms) budget becomes 0, the effect reruns and collects once.
newWorkOrState: One extra tracked read (budget) and one untracked comparison; reruns at drag start/rest (cheap cache hits for exact tiles).
whyOutputsStayIdentical: Conversion, masks, exports and the counting algorithm are untouched; the final count after rest is computed by the same inspect() with the same captured settings. Only the time at which a sampled tile's caption count publishes during an active drag changes (it stays pending with the retained previous result, the existing 'updating' presentation). Exact-size tiles are unaffected.
falsifyingProbe: Done on host: bench/second-performance-audit-2026-10-17/source-review/A/probe-onebit-drag.mjs (loader-hook counter around onebit-usage's mask). Browser falsifier: test-build counter of onebit-usage mask calls during a scripted 60-move Checker threshold drag on 4 x 512^2 sprites (desktop DPR1 and phone). If masks/move ~ 0 in the real app (aborts always precede the yield), reject. Also record renderer CPU, long tasks and rAF gaps during the drag, and caption counts after rest.
risk: Low. Visible change limited to caption timing during drags; sliderDrag rest/resume toggles budget, which restarts collection during pauses (desired). Viewer Tile has budget 0 and is unaffected.

title: Offscreen still tiles convert on every setting change and consume the shared drag budget
workThatDisappears: Conversions (1-bit masks synchronously inside the completedPixels derived; palette previews async) of still tiles scrolled out of view in a scrolling wall, on every settings change and every 1-bit drag move; offscreen tiles also dilute the per-tile drag budget so visible drafts are rougher.
frequency: Every setting change/drag move on scrolling walls (common on phones: 2-3 columns, >6-9 tiles scroll).
expectedBenefit: Work proportional to (N - visible)/N of the wall per change; sharper drafts for visible tiles during drags.
proposedChange: Register wall stills with the existing singleton IntersectionObserver (with a rootMargin of about one viewport), skip conversion while not in view (retaining lastConverted, as offscreen animations already do), convert on entry; divide DRAG_MS by the visible count.
newWorkOrState: One IO registration per wall tile; inView state for stills; visible-count state in App.
whyOutputsStayIdentical: Visible pixels are converted with the same inputs before being shown as current; exports convert full sources independently; counts come from the existing serial queue. Precedent: docs/research/2026-10-12-offscreen-playback.md already holds offscreen animations' frames.
falsifyingProbe: Test-build counter: conversions per setting change split by IO visibility on a 16-sprite phone wall and a 30-sprite desktop wall; renderer CPU per 1-bit drag move. Reject if the offscreen share is small in practical walls or scroll-in staleness is visible.
risk: Medium. Behavior/spec change (draft budget wording, possible one-frame stale art on fast scroll-in); IO edge cases already handled for animations; exact preview count contributions for offscreen stills arrive later via the queue.

title: Third-party Google Fonts stylesheet blocks the module script (App mount) on cold loads
workThatDisappears: Waiting for the fonts.googleapis.com CSS response (DNS/TLS/request; preconnect is in the same head so it barely helps) before any app JS executes; the HTML spec makes deferred/module scripts wait for parser-inserted script-blocking stylesheets. A blackholed Google endpoint delays startup until the request fails.
frequency: Every load without a cached Google CSS response (max-age about a day): first visit (welcome), installed-app cold starts after a day, flaky mobile networks.
expectedBenefit: Earlier first usable control on cold mobile loads (likely one or more network round trips).
proposedChange: Load the font CSS non-blocking (`media="print" onload="this.media='all'"` or `rel=preload as=style` + onload), keep display=swap; make fitPaletteHeader also re-measure on `document.fonts` `loadingdone`.
newWorkOrState: One onload attribute and one fonts event listener.
whyOutputsStayIdentical: No image/export output involved; the fallback-then-swap font behavior already exists via display=swap. Layout re-measurement is RO-driven elsewhere (labelWidth, measureWorkspaceTools).
falsifyingProbe: Built app, cold cache, DevTools Fast/Slow 4G: time to App mount (performance.mark in a test build) and FCP with the current link vs non-blocking link, plus with fonts.googleapis.com request-blocked. Reject if the difference is under about 30 ms on throttled cold loads.
risk: Low-medium: first paint may show fallback font (FOUT), palette-name fit could be stale without the loadingdone hook; needs a visual check in both themes.

title: Eager tooltip DOM per control (popover div + ~12 listeners + aria-describedby) at mount
workThatDisappears: Creating/appending/styling a hidden popover element per tooltip instance until first show; part of the 185-188 ms native paste->Review long task and of tile mounts on large imports.
frequency: Every mount of a control with use:tooltip (editor pages, every imported tile, dock panels).
expectedBenefit: Lower editor Review and batch-import mount cost on phones; magnitude unknown (attribution probe first).
proposedChange: Only after attribution: create the tip lazily on first show while preserving an accessible description from mount (needs an equivalent to aria-describedby; aria-description support must be checked).
newWorkOrState: Lazy element creation path; description mechanism.
whyOutputsStayIdentical: Tooltip text/positioning unchanged; no pixel output involved.
falsifyingProbe: Browser microbench in the built app: render 64 review swatches with the real tooltip action vs a no-op action (same buttons/canvases), measure task duration on desktop and phone. Reject if the tooltip share is under ~10% of the editor long task.
risk: Medium (accessibility contract and tooltip unit tests: src/lib/tooltip.test.js, tooltipCoverage.test.js).

title: Non-passive window-level touch listeners make the whole viewport a blocking touch region
workThatDisappears: Main-thread round trip before scroll start on dock rails, chip rows, the More menu and dialog bodies when the main thread is busy.
frequency: Every touch scroll outside the wall while conversions/imports run.
expectedBenefit: Lower scroll-start latency on non-wall scrollers under load; none for wall scrolling (it still needs the swipe listener).
proposedChange: Attach App's touchmove to the .grid node (swipes only start onWall; touch targets stay fixed for the sequence). Dock's touchstart cannot be made conditional on panel state safely (pointerdown closes the panel before touchstart dispatch); leave it unless a safe lifetime (e.g. until the next touchend) is designed.
whyOutputsStayIdentical: Swipe logic unchanged; listeners receive the same events for touches started on the wall.
falsifyingProbe: Phone CDP touch scroll of the palette rail and PaletteImport body during a busy main thread (import worker publish or 1-bit drag): touchstart to first scroll event latency, window vs .grid listener. Reject if Dock's remaining window touchstart keeps the region blocking or the difference is negligible.
risk: Low-medium (gesture regressions: pull-to-refresh suppression on the wall, dialogs opened mid-gesture).

title: 1-bit color-input drags allocate a fresh full ImageData per tile per input event
workThatDisappears: Per-event allocation of sum(mw*mh*4) bytes (e.g. about 9.7 MB for 12 tiles at 450x450 device px) and the resulting GC.
frequency: Every input event from the native color picker while dragging (continuous on desktop Chrome).
expectedBenefit: Fewer GC pauses during color picking on photo walls; negligible for small sprites.
proposedChange: For still frames, colorize into a retained per-tile buffer and repaint via a version counter instead of identity.
newWorkOrState: Retained buffer per tile (same size as the current one); Pixels repaint trigger.
whyOutputsStayIdentical: colorize writes identical bytes; only buffer identity changes.
falsifyingProbe: Built app, 12-photo 1-bit wall: dispatch 60 input events with varying values to the first color input; DevTools trace GC totals and event handling time. Reject if GC < 5% of handling time.
risk: Medium (lastConverted retention shares the object; animations keep per-frame caches).

title: Opening/closing a panel resamples every large tile twice
workThatDisappears: Reconversion on close for open-look-close cycles (the pre-open result at the original size).
frequency: Each panel toggle on a non-scrolling wall with images larger than their tiles.
expectedBenefit: Instant close without reconversion when no setting changed; nothing when settings changed (common).
proposedChange: Keep one previous-size completed result per tile and reuse it when the inputs and size match again.
newWorkOrState: +1 retained tile-sized frame per sampled tile.
whyOutputsStayIdentical: Reuse only on exact input+size match.
falsifyingProbe: Counter of conversions per panel toggle without edits on a 12-photo wall; phone CPU per toggle. Reject if users rarely toggle without editing or CPU per toggle is small.
risk: Memory growth; spec says keep only the last completed rendering.

title: Preview pan repaints the full-screen checker background every move
workThatDisappears: Viewport-sized background repaint per pan frame (background-position is not compositor-animatable).
frequency: Every pointermove while panning/pinching in Preview.
expectedBenefit: Lower raster/paint per pan frame on phones (DPR 2.25 viewport is ~1.9 M device px).
proposedChange: Paint the checker on a transformed pseudo/child layer moved with transform.
whyOutputsStayIdentical: Same checker phase if the transform equals the current background-position offset.
falsifyingProbe: Phone trace during a scripted pan: Paint+Raster per frame. Reject if under ~1 ms.

title: CanvasGrid observes childList mutations across the whole #app subtree
workThatDisappears: connect() + double rAF + layout reads for unrelated structural mutations (dialogs, tooltips inside dialogs, toast spinner, dock rows).
frequency: Every structural DOM change in the app.
expectedBenefit: Small; only if counts are high in real workflows.
proposedChange: Observe the wall (.grid) and .bar structure only.
whyOutputsStayIdentical: Anchor logic unchanged; only irrelevant triggers removed.
falsifyingProbe: Count MutationObserver callbacks during import of 8 sprites, 10 palette steps with the rail open, and an editor paste->Review. Reject if a few per user action.

title: PaletteImport keeps 256-4096-entry color arrays as deep $state proxies
workThatDisappears: Per-index proxy signal creation/tracking for edited/visible/includes reads.
expectedBenefit: Measured on host: 0.20 ms (256) / 2.3 ms (4096) deep vs 0.008 / 0.052 ms with $state.raw; small vs the 185 ms native editor long task.
risk: Very low; benefit also very low (cleanup-grade).

title: Settings are serialized and written to localStorage on every slider/color input event
workThatDisappears: JSON.stringify of the settings proxy (~1 KB) + setItem per move.
frequency: Every 1-bit style slider and color-input event.
expectedBenefit: Expected well under 0.2 ms per move; likely not worth a change.
proposedChange: Skip writes while `dragging` and write on rest/end.
falsifyingProbe: performance.now around the effect during a 60-move drag in the built app.
risk: Tab close mid-drag loses the last moves.

title: Per-caption backdrop-filter blur during wall scroll
workThatDisappears: One backdrop blur render surface per visible caption per scrolled frame.
proposedChange: Visual/design decision only (opaque caption material when canvas-scrollable).
whyOutputsStayIdentical: Not identical: changes caption appearance; out of scope without design approval.
falsifyingProbe: Phone compositor/GPU trace during fling with many tiles.
risk: Visual change; not an exact optimization.
